Building an app on cd2030.core

Source: vignettes/building-an-app.Rmd
building-an-app.Rmd

The Countdown apps (cd2030.rmncah, cd2030.vaxx, cd2030.pooled) are Shiny front ends to this package. cd2030.core holds everything they share: the app frame, the Load Data screen, the analysis pages, the filters and the report content. An app is a small package that says what is particular to it. This guide describes the parts and how they fit; cd2030.rmncah::run_app() is the complete example.

How the packages fit 

DataSuite
  └─ countdown-analytics                              the DataSuite extension: lists the apps
       └─ cd2030.rmncah / cd2030.vaxx / cd2030.pooled   one R package per app: run_app()
            └─ cd2030.core                            analysis, pages, Load Data screen, report content
                 └─ datasuite.ui                      interface kit, chart options, report builder

datasuite.ui knows nothing about Countdown: it has the components, the page frame and the report engine. cd2030.core plugs Countdown into it. An app adds its indicator group, its pages and its text.

The parts of an app

An app’s run_app() does five things, in this order.

1. Choose the indicator group and the app’s settings 

set_selected_group("rmncah")
options(
  cd2030.app_group = "rmncah",
  cd2030.config = list(
    nat_cov_indicators = c("anc4", "instlivebirths", "penta3", "measles1"),
    consistency_pairs = list(c("anc1", "penta1"), c("penta1", "penta3")),
    has_maternal = TRUE
  )
)

cd2030.config is what the shared pages read to know what to show for this app: which indicators a page offers, which pairs the consistency check compares, whether there is a maternal denominator. A page reads a setting with cd_cfg(), and ?cd_cfg lists the keys.

2. Set up the Load Data screen

The Load Data screen is the same in every app. The fields it asks for (which surveys, which rates) come from options(cd2030.wizard = ...); ?cd_upload_data_ui describes them and the builders for an app’s own fields.

3. Build the translator

Every label is a translation key. The app’s own file is merged with datasuite.ui’s and cd2030.core’s.

i18n <- shiny.i18n::init_i18n(
  translation_json_path = cd_translations(system.file("translation", "translation.json", package = "myapp"))
)
i18n$set_translation_language(language)
cd_use_i18n(i18n)

4. List the pages

A page is a _ui function and a _server function. The app lists every page it has, shared or its own, with the kit’s cd_page_def(): the id, the two functions, and the keys of its title and subtitle.

my_pages <- function() list(
  cd_page_def(
    id = "reporting_rate",
    ui = reporting_rate_ui, server = reporting_rate_server,          # a shared page, from cd2030.core
    title = "title_rr_main", section = "lbl_nav_section_quality", subtitle = "sub_rr_main"
  ),
  cd_page_def(
    id = "my_page",
    ui = my_page_ui, server = my_page_server,                        # a page of the app's own
    title = "title_my_page", section = "lbl_nav_section_analysis", subtitle = "sub_my_page"
  )
)
pages <- my_pages()
cd_use_pages(pages)

The shared pages are listed in the reference under “App: pages”.

5. Build the sidebar and call cd_app()

The sidebar is a list of sections. The standard ones come ready made; cd_nav_section() and cd_nav_item() build others. An item’s tabName is a page’s id.

nav <- list(
  cd_nav_start(),
  cd_nav_quality(),
  cd_nav_denominators(),
  cd_nav_section("lbl_nav_section_analysis",
    cd_nav_national(),
    cd_nav_item("title_my_page", tabName = "my_page", icon = "chart-line", requires_adjustment = TRUE)
  )
)

cd_app(
  app_name = "My app", app_version = "1.0.0", theme = "rmncah",
  nav_sections = nav, registry = pages,
  i18n = i18n, language = language, selected_file = selected_file,
  upload_ui = cd_upload_data_ui, upload_server = cd_upload_data_server
)

cd_app() returns a Shiny app. It adds what is the same everywhere: the header and sidebar, the Introduction and Load Data screens, the row naming the denominators in use, and the dataset, which every page receives as cache. Pages unlock once a dataset is loaded; items with requires_adjustment = TRUE unlock once it is also adjusted.

Writing a page

A page’s _ui function builds its layout from the kit’s components and the shared pieces in this package. Its _server function receives the dataset as a reactive cache and draws from it.

my_page_ui <- function(id, i18n) {
  ns <- shiny::NS(id)
  cd_page_ui(id, i18n = i18n, cd_table_ui(ns("table")))
}

my_page_server <- function(id, cache, i18n) {
  shiny::moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
    cd_table_server("table", data = shiny::reactive(cache()$reporting_rate_national), i18n = i18n)
  })
}

The pieces a page is built from each have a help page, grouped in the reference:

Group What is in it Start at
App: building an app cd_app(), the settings, the guide to the interface ?cd_app, ?"countdown-pages"
App: pages the shared analysis pages, each a _ui / _server pair ?reporting_rate_ui
App: Load Data wizard the Load Data screen, its steps and field builders ?cd_upload_data_ui
App: filters indicator, administrative level, denominator, years ?cd_admin_level_ui
App: layout the dataset header, sidebar sections, scoped pages, tabbed charts ?cd_scope
App: charts and tables chart and table cards with their downloads ?cd_table_ui

Read the source of a shared page that resembles yours before writing one: R/page-reporting_rate.R is a short one. The kit’s own components are described in datasuite.ui (docs/COMPONENTS.md).

Results a page can read

A page should read results from the dataset object, not compute them. Each result is computed once, kept, and cleared when something it depends on changes, so two pages showing the same table do not compute it twice. ?CacheConnection lists them, and cache_definition() says for any of them what it depends on and which pages show it.

Running and publishing

During development, load the app package and call its run_app():

devtools::load_all()
run_app(language = "en")

In DataSuite, the countdown-analytics extension names each app’s package; DataSuite installs the package from r-universe with the extension, and starts run_app() with the chosen file and language. An app’s DESCRIPTION must require the cd2030.core version it needs (cd2030.core (>= 1.4.0)), because DataSuite only updates a package when a newer version is required.
